name: FL Group

summary.text: FL Group was an Icelandic investment company formed in 2005 when Hannes Smarason took over Flugleidir, the holding company of Icelandair, and refashioned it as a leveraged investment company; it was one of the largest shareholders in the bank Glitnir. On May 22, 2007 it announced a $50 million investment in four U.S. real-estate development projects alongside the Bayrock Group, including Trump SoHo in Manhattan, a partnership with Donald Trump and the Sapir Organization. The company was renamed Stodir in mid-2008, delisted from the Icelandic exchange in June 2008, reported a Q2 2008 loss of ISK 11.6 billion driven by its Glitnir stake, and entered administration in September 2008 after the Icelandic government took 75 percent of Glitnir. A 2010 lawsuit by a former Bayrock executive alleged the Bayrock deal was structured to avoid tax; it settled in 2018 without adjudication. The Bayrock file on this site holds the litigation record.

facts.claim: FL Group was formed in 2005 when Hannes Smarason took over Flugleidir, the holding company of Icelandair, sold off assets and redefined the company as a leveraged investment company; it became one of the largest shareholders in the bank Glitnir, whose collapse in 2008 took FL Group down with it.
facts.quote: FL Group was also one of the largest shareholders in the failed bank Glitnir.

facts.claim: The company, renamed Stodir in 2008, reported a Q2 2008 net loss of ISK 11.6 billion (about EUR 97 million), driven mainly by higher cost of capital and a fall in the value of its Glitnir stake, and said its shares had been delisted from the OMX Nordic Exchange Iceland in June 2008.

facts.claim: Stodir entered administration in September 2008 after the Icelandic government took a 75 percent stake in Glitnir, its biggest investment, diluting existing shareholders; its shares passed to creditors in a 2009 restructuring and its assets were sold between 2009 and 2016.
facts.quote: Stodir entered administration in September 2008 after the Icelandic government part-nationalised Glitnir, its biggest investment.

facts.claim: The Daily Telegraph reported in May 2016 that Trump signed documents approving the FL Group deal in 2007 and that the equity investment was later recast as a loan; court filings by former Bayrock finance director Jody Kriss alleged FL Group bought 62 percent of the profits from four Bayrock properties and that the structure was meant to avoid tax. Trump's attorney said Trump had nothing to do with the transaction, and the allegations were settled, not adjudicated.
facts.quote: Trump's attorney disputed this, saying Trump "had nothing to do with the transaction," with his signature merely a formality.

openQuestions: The Stodir administration fact cites Wikipedia alongside PrintWeek; the owner may prefer to drop the Wikipedia source or find the Icelandic court record.
The rename date differs: Wikipedia gives 4 June 2008, the company's Q2 report says July.
The site says FL Group was dissolved in 2014; the sources reached describe administration in 2008 and asset sales through 2016, not a 2014 dissolution.
